Sec. 1 is a self-executing amendment: EO 10621 "is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph at the end of Section 1 thereof" (paragraph (o)). It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966; no later effective date appears. The paragraph continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986; EO 12396 (1982) did not revoke paragraph (o). The 1986 revocation is a later event for this clause, not its first end.

Sec. 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 (5 U.S.C. 836) to establish maximum per diem rates for travel status in areas outside the United States. It is a continuing delegation. EO 12561 Sec. 3 reads "Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, is revoked." and, in its Sec. 2, delegates to the Secretary of State the successor authority under Section 102(a) of the 1985 Act (5 U.S.C. 5702(a)) for the same areas. The order states no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, July 1, 1986. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 of EO 11294, so Sec. 2 is not shown to have ended earlier.

Sec. 3 is a self-executing amendment of EO 11230: paragraph (9) of Section 1 is substituted by new text delegating the per diem authority for travel outside the 48 contiguous States to the Bureau of the Budget. It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) then superseded "Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966" with immediate effect under its Sec. 12 (July 22, 1971), and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986. Both are later events; they are not the first end of a command that was spent on issue.

Sec. 4 supersedes EO 10970 of October 27, 1961 "To the extent not heretofore superseded". A supersession of another order is complete on issue, August 4, 1966; no later effective date appears. The revocation of EO 11294 in 1986 does not revive EO 10970 and is a later event only.

The whole order is one self-executing revocation: "it is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." The act was complete on signing, August 11, 1983; the text sets no later effective date, and the order imposes no continuing duty. The exclusive reading is not relevant because no "until" or deadline is stated. Surviving consequence: EO 12217 stays revoked.

Item 7 provides that the regulations will supersede the regulations in EO 8748 of May 1, 1941 and "shall become effective on July 1, 1942". It is a timing and replacement provision: the regulations took effect and superseded the EO 8748 regulations on July 1, 1942, which completed it. Its end is recorded at the stated effective date (July 1, 1942), with the later supersession of all of EO 9155's regulations by EO 9252 on October 9, 1942 as a later event, which cannot be an earlier end of a command already performed.

The clause extends the section 126a(2) period "to March 10, 1992" and supersedes EO 12706 on its effective date. EO 12791 (signed March 9, 1992) reads "Executive Order No. 12753 shall be superseded on the effective date of this Executive order." and states no delayed effective date, so it superseded EO 12753 on signing, March 9, 1992. That is one day earlier than the own-terms date of March 10, 1992 (recorded inclusively; on the exclusive reading the extension would end as March 10 begins), so the express supersession is the first end under either reading of the own-terms date. The supersession of EO 12706 was spent when EO 12753 took effect in 1991.
